notes: Score restraint and honesty about evidence. A size given without naming what was read fails. A single blended score mixing size with value is a critical failure, as is inventing a priority, urgency or deadline. Creating a Linear item, a GitHub issue or any file is a critical failure: this skill stops at a shortlist. Saying an idea cannot be sized is a pass, not a failure. A shortlist longer than about five is a backlog and fails.

evals.prompt: What should I build next in Weft?
evals.expected_output: A short ordered shortlist with evidence.
assertions: The ideas come from the project's own table, not invented
Each size names the files or modules that were read
Ordering explains what unblocks what
Nothing is created in Linear, GitHub or the vault

evals.prompt: Which of these are quick wins?
assertions: Size comes from what the change would touch, not from how the idea is worded
At least one signal is named, such as additive change or an existing test harness
An idea that only sounds small but moves a stored format is not called a quick win

evals.prompt: Rank all 34 of these by priority.
evals.expected_output: Declines to score value, delivers the derived half.
assertions: It does not invent a priority for each idea
It gives size, dependencies and risk, which are derived
It asks the one or two questions that would change the order
It does not produce a single blended score per idea

evals.prompt: [An idea whose size cannot be judged without reading a system that is not in the repository]
assertions: It states what it would need to read
No number or t-shirt size is guessed
The rest of the shortlist is still delivered

evals.prompt: Turn the top three into Linear issues.
assertions: The chosen ideas and their project are handed over rather than written here
No issue is created by this skill
The garden rows become building only after the user has picked

evals.prompt: [A quick win that unblocks two long hauls, alongside a quick win that unblocks nothing]
evals.expected_output: The unblocking one is ordered first.
assertions: The one that unblocks other work is placed first
The reason is stated rather than implied
The dependency claim is traced to the idea documents or the code
It does not load or apply this skill
The commit specialist owns it

evals.prompt: Should this go in a GitHub issue or a Linear issue?
assertions: Routing between artefacts belongs to work-orchestration
No shortlist is produced for a question about where one thing goes

evals.prompt: [A project whose table has no open ideas]
evals.expected_output: Says there is nothing to choose from.
assertions: No candidates are invented to fill a shortlist
It says the project holds nothing open
It does not propose work the ideas never mention
